files.title: Multiannual Financial Framework 2028–2034
files.status: António Costa tabled his negotiating box on 21 November 2026: €1,582bn in commitments at 2025 prices, €180.6bn below the Commission proposal and €40bn below the Irish Presidency box of 10 October, with slower repayment of NextGenerationEU debt and a digital levy. Leaders discuss it at the Special European Council on 26–27 November and aim for a deal in December. Unanimity in Council, then Parliament's consent; co-rapporteur Siegfried Mureşan called the box unacceptable to Parliament. Three programmes are followed as parts: the European Competitiveness Fund (ITRE co-rapporteurs Christian Ehler and Dan Nica; plenary confirmed ITRE's negotiating mandate on 25 November), the National and Regional Partnership Plans fund (Karlo Ressler, Andrey Novakov and Elsi Katainen; committee vote not before January 2027) and the Performance Regulation (Jean-Marc Germain and Niclas Herbst; more than 1,000 amendments, with the groups split over do no significant harm).

files.title: Digital Omnibus on data: GDPR, ePrivacy, Data Act, NIS2
files.status: The Commission proposed it on 19 November 2025. Coreper II agreed the Council's negotiating mandate on 21 October 2026 (Council doc 14756/26): it keeps the current definition of personal data and adds a provision on pseudonymisation, keeps the ePrivacy cookie rules but drops consent for purposes such as audience measurement and device security, and replaces the single EU incident-reporting entry point with national entry points. In Parliament, the ITRE-LIBE draft report came out on 22 June 2026 and amendments were tabled on 27 July; no committee vote date is set, and talks with the Council start once Parliament has its position. Open fights: personal data and pseudonymisation, AI training on personal data, trade secrets under the Data Act, and the cookie rules.

files.title: Digital Fairness Act
files.status: The Commission adopted the Digital Fairness Act on 11 November 2026, in a consumer package with a Simplification Directive amending the Consumer Rights Directive and a revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation. The DFA is a regulation that replaces the 2005 Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and gives the Commission its own power to investigate and fine, up to 6% of turnover. It targets dark patterns, addictive design, influencer marketing, personalisation that exploits vulnerabilities and misleading pricing, and addresses hard-to-cancel contracts, automatic renewals and free trials that turn into paid subscriptions. The social media minimum age sits in the EU KIDS Act, which nodo follows as its own file. Parliament's committee referral and rapporteur, and the Council working party, are still to come.

files.title: Technology Sovereignty Package: Chips Act 2.0 and Cloud and AI Development Act
files.status: The Commission proposed both on 3 June 2026. In Parliament, ITRE leads the Chips Act 2.0 (rapporteur Oliver Schenk, appointed 31 August) and ITRE and IMCO share the CADA (Diego Solier and Reinier van Lanschot); neither has a draft report or a committee vote date yet. The Council's industry working party took up the Chips Act 2.0 on 2 September and on 12 and 13 October, and had the Presidency compromise text (doc 13545/26 REV 1) on its agenda on 29 and 30 October. On the CADA, the telecoms working party had the Presidency's first compromise text of Title IV on 10 November and took up the text on Pillars 1 and 2 (doc 15830/26) on 24 November. The CADA aims to triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years and creates a framework to assess cloud and AI sovereignty, which is the most contested element.

files.title: AI Act implementation after the Digital Omnibus on AI
files.status: The Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, was signed on 8 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July. Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 and Annex I obligations from 2 August 2028. On 2 December 2026 the new prohibitions apply (AI that generates non-consensual intimate imagery or child sexual abuse material), and generative AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must meet the marking duty of Article 50(2).

files.title: European Grids Package: TEN-E regulation and permitting directive
files.lede: Permitting deal reached on 18 November; the final TEN-E trilogue is expected in early December.
files.status: The Commission proposed both on 10 December 2025; the Council agreed general approaches on 26 June 2026, and Parliament's mandates (ITRE reports by Niels Fuglsang on permitting and Tsvetelina Penkova on TEN-E) were confirmed in plenary on 8 July and 16 September. Council and Parliament reached a provisional agreement on the permitting directive early on 18 November 2026, at the third trilogue: permits for solar with co-located storage and grid connections within three months, stand-alone storage and recharging points within six, and a benefit-sharing threshold cut from 10 to 7 MW (Council press release); ITRE, plenary and the Council must still endorse it. On TEN-E, the third trilogue on 10 November settled the framework assessment, while congestion income stays open; Agence Europe reports the final round for early December. The European Council asked the co-legislators to agree the package in 2026.

files.lede: Seven trilogues, no deal: merchant exceptions, payment-provider fees, the roll-out and the holding limit are still open.
files.status: The Commission proposed it in June 2023. The Council agreed its position on 19 December 2025. Parliament's ECON adopted Fernando Navarrete's report on 23 June 2026 and plenary confirmed the mandate on 9 July. Trilogues are under way: the fifth, on 20 October, covered offline payment limits, anti-money-laundering rules for small payments and the long-term operating model; the sixth, on 5 November, and the seventh, overnight on 18–19 November, ended without a political agreement (Agence Europe). Still open: exceptions to mandatory merchant acceptance, the remuneration model for payment providers, the staggered roll-out and who sets the holding limit; 3 and 16 December are suggested for further trilogues and the Council wants the file closed before the end of the year (Agence Europe). The ECB aims for issuance from 2029 if the law passes.

files.title: EU KIDS Act: minimum age for social media and safety by design for minors
files.lede: No social media under 13, parent-managed mini accounts at 13–14, own accounts from 15. IMCO leads; no rapporteur yet.
files.status: The Commission proposed the EU KIDS Act on 17 September 2026 (COM(2026)681). Children under 13 could not use social media; at 13 and 14 only through mini accounts managed by a parent, with limited features and one hour a day; from 15 with their own account. Social media and video-sharing platforms would verify age when an account is opened and check existing accounts within six months. Safety-by-design duties cover social media, video-sharing, online games, AI companions and chatbots used by under-18s. The Observatory lists Stéphane Séjourné and DG GROW as responsible; Henna Virkkunen presented the proposal with the President. In the Council, the Audiovisual and Media Working Party has examined it since 2 October. In Parliament, IMCO leads, with opinions from SANT, ITRE, CULT, JURI and LIBE; CULT named Maria Guzenina (S&D) to draft its opinion. No IMCO rapporteur yet.

files.title: EU Inc.: the 28th regime corporate legal framework
files.lede: René Repasi (S&D) leads in JURI. ECON and EMPL opinions are adopted; the JURI vote has no date yet.
files.status: The Commission proposed EU Inc. on 18 March 2026 (COM(2026)321): an optional EU-wide corporate legal form, the "28th regime", for companies operating across borders. It is on the 2027 priority list. JURI leads with René Repasi (S&D) as rapporteur; his draft report was tabled on 29 June and amendments on 22 July. ECON adopted its opinion on 15 July and EMPL on 10 September.

files.title: European Business Wallets
files.lede: In trilogue since 14 October. Eero Heinäluoma (S&D) leads for Parliament.
files.status: The Commission proposed the European Business Wallets regulation on 19 November 2025 (COM(2025)838): digital wallets for businesses and public bodies to identify themselves, sign and exchange documents across the EU. It is on the 2027 priority list. ITRE adopted the report by Eero Heinäluoma (S&D) on 10 September, with opinions from IMCO and JURI. Plenary confirmed the negotiating mandate on 7 October and the first trilogue took place on 14 October.

files.title: Fair labour mobility package: Skills Portability Act, European Labour Authority, ESSPASS and recognition of qualifications
files.lede: Five proposals from 15 September. On the Skills Portability Act, Brigitte van den Berg (Renew) leads in EMPL.
files.status: The Commission proposed the fair labour mobility package on 15 September 2026: a Skills Portability Act (COM(2026)992), a revised mandate for the European Labour Authority, digital social security coordination with the European Social Security Pass (ESSPASS), digital recognition of professional qualifications, and recognition of third-country nationals' qualifications. All five are on the 2027 priority list. On the Skills Portability Act, referred on 22 October, EMPL leads with Brigitte van den Berg (Renew); IMCO and CULT give opinions.

files.title: Environmental omnibus (Omnibus VIII): faster environmental assessments, INSPIRE, extended producer responsibility and batteries
files.lede: Parliament voted the environmental assessments report by Emma Ytterell (Renew) in plenary on 25 November.
files.status: The Commission proposed the environmental omnibus on 10 December 2025: faster environmental assessments (COM(2025)984), changes to the INSPIRE spatial data rules and an environmental directive, simpler extended producer responsibility for waste, packaging and batteries, and amendments to the batteries regulations. All are on the 2027 priority list. On environmental assessments, ENVI adopted the report by Emma Ytterell (Renew) on 4 November and Parliament voted on it in plenary on 25 November (text adopted TA-10-2026-0394).
